The RL approach is validated against Exhaustive Search (when feasible) and Ant Colony Optimization, and against two simple baselines, i.e. Ascending Sorting and Descending Sorting. The results of the numerical experiments demonstrate that RL effectively identifies optimal and near-optimal transfer sequences, matching the performance of traditional metaheuristics, and offering a framework for rapid mission planning in orbital environment.

papers.title: Covariance Estimation for Orbit Determination with Physics-Informed Extreme Learning Machines
papers.authors: Benedikt Aigner, Fabian Dallinger, Thomas Andert, Roger Förstner
papers.abstract: Physics-Informed Extreme Learning Machines (PIELMs) are an efficient alternative to classical orbit determination by combining measurement fitting with explicit enforcement of the equations of motion. Practical applications, however, also require uncertainty information. This paper investigates a covariance estimation procedure for PIELM-based orbit determination that propagates assumed measurement noise through the trained model to obtain time-varying position uncertainties. We compute an output-weight covariance from the Jacobian of the stacked residuals with respect to the learned output weights and map it via linear covariance propagation to a time-resolved 3×3 position covariance along the reconstructed trajectory. Using a controlled groundstation tracking scenario over a single orbital arc, we compare the resulting 1σ envelopes against a classical batch weighted least-squares (WLS) reference. Covariance behaviour is assessed by Monte Carlo ensembles over measurement-noise realizations and over random hidden-layer initializations, using the normalized estimation error squared and empirical ellipsoidal coverage. The results indicate that the proposed method yields structured, time-varying uncertainty estimates whose magnitudes are broadly consistent with the realized errors, while exhibiting a systematic time dependence in the calibration along the arc.

papers.title: SYNDAQ: Synthetic Data Generation and Qualification
papers.authors: Jose Martinez, Andrea Gobbi, Satish Madhogaria, Patrick Fleith, Kevin Rojczyk, Aiden Ahmet Erdogan, Davide Molinari, Simone Toso, Florian Ehmann, Marco Cristoforetti, Evridiki Ntagiou
papers.abstract: Synthetic data is increasingly important for machine learning in domains where real-world data is scarce, sensitive, imbalanced, or costly to obtain. By generating realistic and controllable datasets, it enables robust training, improves performance on rare cases, and supports privacypreserving development. In this work, we investigate synthetic data generation methods across space operations use cases spanning multiple modalities: documentation (text), telemetry (time series), and optical telescope imagery. We report results and lessons learned from applying these methods in operationally relevant scenarios.

papers.title: AI-based Classification of Simulated Cosmic Radiation Bit Upsets into the SRAMs of a Commercial-grade FPGA
papers.authors: Artur Kazak, Stefan Popa, Andrei Bertescu, Mihai Ivanovici
papers.abstract: Commercial-grade SRAM-based FPGAs can be qualified for space applications. For instance, they can serve as radiation sensors by periodically scanning their SRAMs for bit upsets. However, existing implementations lose data when the upset rates exceed the telemetry buffer capacity, precisely during high-intensity events that are most relevant for analysis. We present an enhanced architecture that integrates on-chip neural-network-based classification with per-element telemetry aggregation. A lightweight multi-layer perceptron (MLP) classifies every pair of detected bit upsets within each scan cycle, distinguishing singlecell from multiple-cell upsets without prior architecture-specific calibration. In synthetic experiments, the MLP achieves F1 scores between 0.92 and 0.97 on structured bitinterleaving physical layouts and up to 0.72 with perfect recall on a previously unseen layout. This aggregation reduces the buffer overflow occurrence. We compare our method with an offset-histogram method from the literature. The two classifiers exhibit nearly identical resource footprints, but only the MLP operates without calibration.

papers.title: SPACE-KBP: A Dataset for End-to-End Knowledge Base Population in the Space Mission Domain
papers.authors: José Manuel Gómez-Pérez, Cristian Berrío, Andrés García-Silva
papers.abstract: We present SPACE-KBP, to the best of our knowledge the first dataset for end-to-end knowledge base population (KBP) in the space mission domain. The dataset is constructed from textual mission descriptions and structured domain resources, and is aligned with the ESA space mission ontology. It provides paired inputs and outputs for generating ontology-compliant RDF triples, enabling the training and evaluation of large language models (LLMs) for end-to-end KBP. As a case study, we use SPACE-KBP to populate a space mission knowledge graph by fine-tuning LLMs of varying sizes. Our experiments show that compact, domain-specialized models achieve competitive, and in some cases superior, performance compared with larger models. Furthermore, after fine-tuning on SPACE-KBP, the models no longer require explicit ontology descriptions in the prompt, indicating that the required ontology knowledge is effectively captured during fine-tuning. These findings show that compact models and shorter prompts improve deployment efficiency while reducing computational cost for domain-specific KBP.

papers.title: Stellar Apps: software execution platform for AI in space
papers.authors: Arnau Prat, Armin Purle-Kopacz, Hendrik Otte, Daniel Lüdtke
papers.abstract: The increased complexity of space missions, coupled with emerging trends such as long-duration missions and large satellite constellations, demands new approaches to autonomy and on-board data handling. Artificial Intelligence (AI), and in particular Machine Learning (ML), is a key enabler of on-board autonomy and data processing in space systems. However, deploying AI applications on-board spacecraft poses significant challenges in terms of safety, cybersecurity, and resource usage constraints, to name a few. This paper presents Stellar Apps, a software platform designed to enable the safe and secure execution of untrusted third-party applications, including AI-based ones, on spacecraft computers. Stellar Apps provides isolation, multi-tenancy, real-time support, and access to AI accelerators, while enabling incremental in-orbit updates. In this paper, we discuss how Stellar Apps facilitates the execution of AI applications in space.

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning-Optimized Sensor Placement for Boosting Large-Scale Surrogate Hydrological Models
papers.authors: Amir Aieb, Miguel Pincheira, Massimo Vecchio, Fabio Antonelli
papers.abstract: Reliable estimation of potential evapotranspiration (PET) over large spatial domains is challenged by sparse observations, heterogeneous terrain, and the computational cost of physically based models. This work introduces a technique for selecting representative sensor locations and training a 3DCNN surrogate model for accurate large-scale gridded PET prediction. To address the sensor-placement challenge, we reframe sensor data as a pixel-selection problem within the reinforcement-learning (RL) workflow. Using SRTM elevation and CHELSA temperature inputs across Italian catchments, the RL-based approach improves spatial alignment in XGBoost-selected pixels by over 70%. Moreover, it optimises and preserves the data pattern using only 2% of the full pixels. The resulting technique enhances predictive performance of surrogate model compared to the baseline methods and supports scalable, spatially coherent PET estimation under data-sparse conditions.

papers.title: Uncertainty-Aware Surrogate Modeling of Thrust Vectoring Performance in Differentially Throttled Linear Aerospike Nozzles
papers.authors: Bernard Postrach
papers.abstract: Differential throttling enables gimbal-free thrust vector control in linear aerospike nozzles. However, high-fidelity CFD remains prohibitively expensive for iterative design and control. Three uncertainty-aware surrogate models— Gaussian process regression (composite anisotropic RBF + rational quadratic kernel), Support Vector Regression (RBF kernel), and Polynomial Ridge Regression (L2-regularized polynomial expansion)—were trained on steady 2D RANS linear aerospike simulations. The input parameter space (inlet pressure, throttle ratio, ambient pressure) was sampled using two-stage Latin hypercube sampling. Axial and lateral thrust components were predicted independently, with epistemic uncertainty quantified from GPR posterior variance or bootstrapped ensembles (SVR, PRR). Repeated 10-fold cross-validation demonstrates high predictive effectiveness for all surrogates with Gaussian process regression achieving the lowest mean absolute error in both thrust magnitude and thrust vector angle across sparse training sets, while delivering well-calibrated ±3σ bounds with high empirical coverage of test and cross-validation points. The resulting surrogates provide rapid, confidence-aware predictions that bridge high-fidelity aerodynamics and mission-oriented thrust vector control applications.

papers.title: Reducing false positives in wide-field astronomical streak detection using a lightweight CNN classifier
papers.authors: Vincent Fiszbin, Elisabeth Rachith, Andrew Price, Stephan Hellmich, Mathieu Salzmann
papers.abstract: Satellites and orbital debris crossing a telescope’s field of view leave linear streaks on long-exposure images. These streaks contain information on object orbit, size, and rotation. Streaks found in astronomical archives can thus be exploited for the benefit of Space Situational Awareness (SSA). We build upon an existing deep-learning streak detection pipeline applied to the VLT Survey Telescope (VST) archive. While accurate at localizing streak endpoints, the detector produces a high false positive rate on previously unseen data, preventing reliable large-scale processing. We introduce a lightweight post-detection classifier trained on manually annotated VST cutouts to filter detector outputs. On a withheld test month of archival data, the classifier rejects 96% of false positives while preserving 97% of true streaks, increasing the pipeline F1-score from 0.87 to 0.98. We conduct a systematic study to identify the most effective data representation and model architecture. A lightweight VGG6 convolutional neural network achieves the highest validation performance, while deeper residual models do not provide measurable gains. A multilayer perceptron using only numerical features produced by the detector enables faster inference but at reduced accuracy. The resulting pipeline enables reliable full-archive processing and a more comprehensive analysis of the detected streaks, potentially including uncatalogued debris.

papers.title: Towards Automated Grain Size Analysis for ExoMars: Preliminary Results from the GRAINS Project
papers.authors: Cristina Luna, Almudena Moreno, Augusto Gómez Eguíluz, Guillermo Algarabel, Sergio Álvarez, Joanna Kozakiewicz, Alexander M. Barrett, Jean-Luc Josset, Elena A. Favaro, Elliot Sefton-Nash
papers.abstract: Grain size is a fundamental descriptor of sedimentary material. For the ExoMars Rosalind Franklin Rover, it carries direct relevance to the search for preserved organic matter at Oxia Planum. However, laboratory sieving and manual photosieving are both incompatible with the operational timeline of the mission, making automated image-based granulometry a necessity rather than a convenience. This paper reviews the progression of image-based grain size methods with emphasis on deep learning segmentation, and identifies the ImageGrains 2.0 framework as the most suitable current approach for planetary deployment. We describe its adaptation within the GRAINS project, including the camera and illumination setup used to acquire PanCam and CLUPI representative analogue imagery, and present preliminary segmentation and grain size results obtained on a dataset of 21 Antarctic analogue samples that is now being extended to further Mars analogue materials.

papers.title: From Ground to In-Orbit: Enabling Real-Time On-Board Anomaly Detection with ATHMoS
papers.authors: Kathrin Helmsauer, Clemens Schefels, Leonard Schlag, Christian Stirm
papers.abstract: The Automated Telemetry Health Monitoring System (ATHMoS) has been operational at the German Space Operations Center (GSOC) since 2022 as a semi-supervised novelty detection framework for spacecraft telemetry, enabling the detection of previously unseen system states without labeled anomaly data. This paper presents the systematic transformation of ATHMoS from a batch-oriented ground analysis tool to a real-time onboard implementation (ATHMoS-RT). We introduce architectural and algorithmic adaptations that enable deployment at the edge under strict safety and computational constraints, while preserving statistical traceability and human oversight. A comparative analysis of ground and onboard configurations reveals how simplified workflows can maintain reliable detection despite limited compute resources. This transition significantly reduces the time-to-detection by removing dependencies on ground-station contact, allowing operators to prepare for anomalies in real-time before the next scheduled satellite pass.

papers.title: Online Learning for Dynamic Constellation Topologies
papers.authors: João Norberto, Ricardo N. Ferreira, Cláudia Soares
papers.abstract: The use of satellite networks has increased significantly in recent years due to their advantages over purely terrestrial systems, such as higher availability and coverage. However, to effectively provide these services, satellite networks must cope with the continuous orbital movement and maneuvering of their nodes and the impact on the network’s topology. In this work, we address the problem of (dynamic) network topology configuration under the online learning framework. As a byproduct, our approach does not assume structure about the network, such as known orbital planes (that could be violated by maneuvering satellites). We empirically demonstrate that our problem formulation matches the performance of state-of-the-art offline methods. Importantly, we demonstrate that our approach is amenable to constrained online learning, exhibiting a trade-off between computational complexity per iteration and convergence to a final strategy.

papers.title: Transformer attention as a domain clustering tool for space survey machine learning pipelines
papers.authors: Saamie Helena Vincken
papers.abstract: Modern astronomical surveys generate imaging datasets containing billions of objects, requiring automated machine learning (ML) pipelines. As survey sizes increase, analyzing these datasets at full scale becomes increasingly challenging. Methods that can group visually similar objects and reduce large datasets through clustering are therefore of practical importance. In this work we investigate the clustering behavior of embeddings produced by transformer based vision models. Controlled experiments are performed using images from the Euclid Space Telescope, with three architectures being compared: a ResNet-50 convolutional neural network (CNN); a vision transformer (ViT); and a ViT fine-tuned on Euclid data. Feature embeddings are analyzed using uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP) across multiple experiments including galaxy morphology separation, star–galaxy separation, simulated versus real observation separation, and larger randomly selected sets. The results show that transformer embeddings often produce clear separated clusters corresponding to meaningful domains. This suggests that transformer embeddings could be used as a pre- or postfiltering step in survey pipelines, reducing the volume of data that requires expensive inspection or further machine learning analysis.

papers.title: A Cross-Task Analysis of Post-Training Quantization Robustness in Earth Observation
papers.authors: Franz Figueroa, César Cabezas, Jose Carlos Salinas, Gonzalo Alvis
papers.abstract: Deploying deep neural networks onboard Earth Observation (EO) platforms requires model compression strategies that reduce memory footprint and computational cost without compromising task performance. Post-training quantization (PTQ) is a deployment-viable approach, yet its robustness across different EO task types remains insufficiently characterized. This work evaluates the algorithmic robustness of static INT8 PTQ across three EO tasks—scene-level classification, object-level detection, and pixel-level semantic segmentation—using a shared ResNet-50 backbone and backbone-only quantization as a controlled compression strategy. Evaluation is performed on EuroSAT, DIOR, and LoveDA, with model size reduction and compression ratio reported as hardware-agnostic efficiency indicators. Results show that quantization sensitivity differs across the evaluated EO task types: scene classification and semantic segmentation exhibit limited degradation under backbone-only INT8 PTQ, while object detection with Faster R-CNN shows substantially higher sensitivity at a reduced compression ratio. This behavior may be associated with error propagation across the two-stage pipeline, suggesting that architectural factors may contribute beyond spatial prediction granularity alone. These results provide a baseline for assessing the trade-offs of INT8 PTQ across EO task types in resource-constrained onboard systems.

papers.title: A Data-Driven Framework For Space-Tailored State Of Health Battery Management System
papers.authors: Roberto Giovanni Sbarra, Michele Pasquali, Giuliano Coppotelli, Paolo Gaudenzi, Davide di Ienno, Carlo Ciancarelli, Gianluca Furano, Livia Manovi, Mihalis Tourloukis
papers.abstract: The evolution of distributed space systems is increasingly mirroring the architectural transformation of modern automotive embedded systems, moving from rigid, hardware-centric designs to software-defined, intelligent platforms. In this shifting landscape, the development of autonomous satellite units requires onboard processing and decision-support capabilities to ensure service continuity while reducing the high costs associated with groundsegment operations. Central to these distributed architectures are energy storage subsystems; specifically, lithiumion batteries, which are subject to highly non-linear degradation and must be monitored with extreme precision under the harsh thermal and radiation environments of space. To address these challenges, this work introduces a State of Health (SOH) monitoring framework based on a supervised Machine Learning algorithm. The model is evaluated under different operating conditions to analyze its generalization ability. Recognizing the stringent computing power and storage constraints typical of space-grade hardware, the algorithm is optimized using pruning and quantization techniques, allowing sophisticated inference to run on resource-constrained microcontrollers. Finally, a specialized BMS architecture is proposed to host these compressed algorithms, providing a holistic solution that combines a predictive model with a real-world architectural blueprint. This study contributes to the realization of advanced, autonomous health monitoring for the next generation of distributed space missions.

papers.title: Differentiable Mascons: A Spatial–Mass Joint Optimization Framework for Asteroid Gravity Inversion
papers.authors: Yaqiong Wang, Daniel Hestroffer, Huan Xie
papers.abstract: Accurate gravity-field reconstruction around irregular small bodies is critical for safe close-proximity operations in deep-space missions. Classical mascon models are physically interpretable but are tied to static grids, limiting their ability to represent localized high-frequency anomalies without heavy discretization. Implicit neural gravity representations can be accurate, yet are often expensive for dense evaluation and may exhibit near-surface artifacts. We propose Differentiable Mascons (DM), a physicsconstrained spatial–mass joint optimization framework for explicit asteroid gravity inversion. DM liberates mascons from rigid grids and jointly optimizes their masses and 3D coordinates using differentiable gravity residuals. Physical validity is ensured by construction via a smooth non-negative mass parameterization and a shape-informed optimizer-state pruning strategy that keeps mascons inside the target body. A gradient-driven adaptive resampling mechanism further reallocates mascons toward high-error regions to better capture localized anomalies. Experiments on a highly heterogeneous asteroid benchmark across multiple orbital altitudes show that DM consistently outperforms static-grid mascons and implicitnetwork baselines, reducing far-field relative errors by up to an order of magnitude. Visualizations also indicate improved recovery of salient internal heterogeneity in our synthetic experiments.

papers.title: Accelerating Integer-Quantized AI and Related Workloads in a Space-Grade Multicore Processor via SWAR ISA Extensions
papers.authors: Martin Daněk, Roman Bartosinski, Carl Nettelblad, Fredrik Hellman, Daniel Cederman, Johan Klockars, Pablo Ghiglino, Rafael Tordoya, Lucana Santos, Roland Weigand
papers.abstract: This paper describes how SIMD Within A Register (SWAR) custom instruction set architecture extensions have been added to the GR765 multicore RISC-V/SPARC space-grade processor. These extensions help speed up low-precision quantized arithmetic operations, which are common in AI workloads. The work also covers changes made to the software stack, compiler, and debugging support that allow SWAR to be used. Benchmark results show a performance boost for typical space-related applications, including those based on machine learning, when SWAR is activated. Additionally, for the AI components, we present a space-qualified inference engine that has a modular mathematical backend that relies on the concept of micro-kernels to implement deep neural network operators for a RISC-V core (NOEL-V) and SWAR, showing the speedup achieved on the OBPMark-ML performance framework when SWAR is enabled.

papers.title: MANUSAT: Onboard Edge AI Health Monitoring for CMG Bearing Fault Detection
papers.authors: Eleonora Mariotti, Gianluca Furano, Andrea Zanellini, Riccardo Zanella, Mattia Violi, Kevin Russo, Francesco Aldrigo, Riccardo Rovatti, Mauro Mangia
papers.abstract: Early-stage bearing faults in satellite Control Moment Gyroscopes (CMGs) produce high-frequency vibration signatures that cannot be captured through conventional lowrate telemetry and are impractical to downlink due to bandwidth limitations. This paper presents MANUSAT, an edge-computing health monitoring architecture that detects CMG anomalies directly onboard the spacecraft. The system integrates six-axis vibration sensing with an Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA)-based processing unit performing signal acquisition and machine learning inference at the edge. Anomaly detection relies on convolutional autoencoder models trained exclusively on nominal vibration data, using Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) spectrograms as input. The approach is validated on an experimental testbed featuring a modified CMG with an artificially induced outer-race bearing defect. Both model variants achieve perfect class separation, i.e., Area Under the Curve (AUC) = 1, on severe faults; sensitivity to weaker anomalies is further improved by a moving-average confirmation strategy. Deployment on a Commercial Off-The- Shelf (COTS) PolarFire SoC FPGA yields an inference latency of 70 ms, confirming real-time onboard feasibility.

papers.title: Early Detection of Satellite Telemetry Data Anomalies using Hyperdimensional Computing
papers.authors: Benjamin Scott, Tajana Rosing, Flavio Ponzina
papers.abstract: Spacecraft operations depend on continuous telemetry streams to assess subsystem health, yet most anomaly detectors are reactive, raising alarms only after anomalous samples appear. We present SatAnomHD, a prediction-driven pipeline for early detection of satellite telemetry anomalies using hyperdimensional computing (HDC). SatAnomHD encodes each telemetry channel with permutation–level hypervectors that preserve temporal order and continuous values, and trains a multivariate HDC autoregressor to forecast S future samples per channel. Predicted trajectories are re-encoded via random projection and scored by a lightweight binary HDC classifier to estimate anomaly probability within a tunable horizon, providing tens-ofseconds to minutes of lead time. HDC learning uses simple, gradient-free operations with incremental updates, enabling efficient inference and on-board finetuning under CubeSat-class power and memory limits. We evaluate SatAnomHD on the ESA Anomaly Detection Benchmark (ESA- ADB), Mission1, spanning 14 years of operations. Across horizons from 30 s to 5 min ahead, SatAnomHD matches the alarm precision of the current state of the art while delivering up to 60×/230× faster and 56×/206× more energy-efficient inference/training, shifting detection from reactive scoring to predictive early warning.

papers.title: Boosting Sentinel-2 Crop Disease Classification via Self-Supervised Pretraining: A Comparative Study of CNN and SwinV2 Backbones
papers.authors: Salvatore Cassano, Alessandra Costantino, Silvia Rainò, Francesco Giordano, Alexey Petrushin, Franco Maria Battagello
papers.abstract: Satellite imagery can deliver timely, scalable insights to farmers and cooperatives, enabling early detection of crop stress and disease before symptoms become evident at field level. Motivated by the Beyond Visible Spectrum AI for Agriculture 2026 Kaggle challenge, we investigated a practical end-to-end pipeline that converts raw multi-spectral Sentinel-2 patches into actionable disease-class predictions. The task consists of classifying four categories (Aphid, Blast, Rice Plant Hopper (RPH), Rust) from per-band Geo- TIFF inputs (B1–B12). To assess design choices under class imbalance and acquisition variability, we perform a controlled comparison between a convolutional backbone and a hierarchical Transformer backbone, and evaluate the impact of self-supervised masked pretraining on downstream performance. Models are fine-tuned with class-weighted crossentropy. Finally, we leveraged an Explainable AI technique to attribute predictions to spatial regions and spectral bands, supporting the interpretability of the architectures. Results show that self-supervised pretraining can improve classification performance, with clearer gains for the SwinV2 backbone than for ResNet-18. Explainability analysis qualitatively confirms that the architecture considered focuses on specific regions of the field, taking its decisions with varying degrees of confidence (the self-supervised-initialised one is more confident). Furthermore, this analysis shows how the best-performing net focuses on the relevant agronomic bands. Potential limits of the study so far conducted and further research directions are illustrated in the Discussion section.

papers.title: Rapid Prediction of Exoplanetary Cloud Properties via Autoencoders
papers.authors: Amit Reza, Zlata Zelenska, Ludmila Carone, Christiane Helling
papers.abstract: Cloud formation modeling is a crucial frontier for understanding atmospheric composition, dynamics, and the potential habitability (i.e., biosignature) of exoplanets. The formation of cloud particles is determined by local gas temperature, gas density, and gas composition, and hence traces the local thermodynamic conditions. The relevant cloud properties include mean particle size, cloud particle number density, material volume fractions, and depleted element abundances for the elements that participate in the cloud formation process, which are required for solving the radiative transfer. These cloud properties are computed from one-dimensional local pressure-temperature profiles obtained from a three-dimensional general circulation model (GCM). Computing cloud properties involves solving a complex time-dependent reaction-diffusion equation, which is computationally intensive. To reduce these computational costs, we present a neural network (NN) emulator that maps atmospheric parameters to cloud properties via a latent-space representation learned by an autoencoder. By leveraging multiple specialized NN branches for inhomogeneous data, this approach efficiently predicts cloud properties, achieving high accuracy on a GCM grid of 10 hot Jupiters. This generative approach shows high prediction accuracy for cloud properties at lower global temperatures. At higher global temperatures, increased prediction errors are expected, reflecting the greater complexity of cloud formation in these regimes.

papers.title: Automated Satellite Conjunction Management with Transformer-Based Bayesian Deep Learning Approach
papers.authors: Amirah Almutairi, Jana Redaini, Rana Alzahrani, Mai Fadel
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of satellite mega-constellations in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) has increased the frequency of conjunction events, creating a need for reliable collision-risk assessment tools. Conjunction Data Messages (CDMs) provide sequential updates during close approaches, but their analysis is challenging due to orbital uncertainty and the increasing volume of conjunction data. This paper proposes an uncertainty-aware framework for Next-CDM prediction using a Transformer Encoder (TE) architecture. The TE leverages self-attention to capture temporal dependencies across CDM sequences and is evaluated as an alternative to recurrent architectures for modeling successive conjunction updates. The framework integrates Monte Carlo (MC) Dropout for epistemic uncertainty estimation and conformal calibration to improve the reliability of predictive intervals. The framework is evaluated against LSTM, GRU, and Last-CDM baselines using the ESA Kelvins dataset and the Aldoria dataset. The TE achieved the lowest deterministic mean squared error (MSE) on both datasets, with values of 0.1566 on Kelvins and 0.1061 on Aldoria, while also attaining the strongest uncertainty ranking and requiring fewer trainable parameters than the recurrent baselines. Computationally, the TE achieved faster inference on the larger Kelvins workload. Overall, the results demonstrate the potential of the TE for accurate and uncertainty-aware Next-CDM prediction.
